heading: Benefits of outdoor activities for young children
points: Movement and coordination: Active games and tricycle play give children opportunities to practise balance, steering and moving confidently through a shared space.
Taking turns and teamwork: Group activities encourage children to wait, listen to simple instructions and enjoy playing alongside their friends.
Curiosity and independence: Exploring beyond the classroom invites children to notice their surroundings, make choices and try something new with encouragement.
Communication through play: Shared games give children reasons to ask questions, explain ideas and celebrate small achievements together.

seoText: At Kids Planet Play School & Day Care, outdoor activities complement classroom learning for children aged 2–6. Families looking for a play school in Old Town BBSR can explore these photographs for a glimpse of our school community. We offer Preschool, Nursery, LKG and UKG, with daycare for all four age groups. Contact us to discuss admissions or arrange a visit.

heading: Benefits of cultural activities and celebrations
points: Creative expression: Dressing up, drama and festive activities give children different ways to express ideas through movement, colour and imagination.
Confidence in participation: Joining a celebration offers opportunities to take a small role, try a performance and share a moment with friends and teachers.
Discovering traditions: Occasions such as Independence Day, Janmashtami and Ganesh Puja introduce children to stories, symbols and celebrations in an approachable way.
Belonging and appreciation: Teachers’ Day and shared school events create opportunities to thank others, join in together and build happy memories.

heading: Benefits of classroom activities in the early years
points: Fine motor practice: Drawing, colouring and handling classroom materials give children opportunities to practise small hand movements and develop familiarity with everyday learning tools.
Language and listening: Talking with teachers and classmates helps children practise describing their work, asking questions and listening to one another.
Attention and problem-solving: Creative tasks encourage children to explore colours and shapes, make choices and stay with an activity at their own pace.
Comfort with school routines: Shared classroom experiences offer practice in taking turns, working alongside friends and becoming familiar with a learning environment.
